q: Cubical type theory (Bezem-Coquand-Huber, CCHM) provides a computational interpretation of HoTT where:
opts: The univalence axiom has no computational content
The univalence axiom is provable from cubical primitives (faces, degeneracies, connections in the n-cube) and has a reduction rule (is definitionally true)
Cubical types are just simplicial types
Higher inductive types are not definable
exp: Cubical type theory (CTT): introduces an interval type I with endpoints 0, 1 and face maps. Paths are functions I → A; the composition/filling operations give a constructive proof of univalence (as a theorem, not an axiom). This resolves the 'non-constructive' nature of the original HoTT book.
